A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Kaleido research work. All 27 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: v2 reports original architecture ablations, novel-view synthesis, camera-conditioned video generation, 3D reconstruction and efficiency measurements in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the ablations in Appendix A and the additional performance and efficiency results in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The Kaleido architecture, positional encoding, training objectives, sampling strategies, register tokens and frame-interpolation procedure in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation datasets, tasks and tested scenarios are unchanged. Both versions already cover the reference-to-target configurations documented in Appendix A; the Figure 3 caption correction adds no scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including SV3D, EscherNet and SEVA for view synthesis; MotionCtrl, VD3D, ViewCrafter and Wonderland for video; and the reconstruction and efficiency baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 3's caption changes its stated first evaluation setting from five reference views and one target to one reference view and five targets. This is a limited correction to the reported protocol: the unchanged plot headings and Appendix A's Table 5 already support the latter setting, so it does not establish changed or rerun experiments.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix A retain the same architecture ablations, activation analyses and sampling comparisons. The Figure 3 caption correction changes neither the questions tested nor the evidence presented.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including point estimates and averaged latency measurements. Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including Tables 2–5 and 7–8. Figure 3 retains identical values and column headings despite its corrected caption.

T1.justification: The conditional formulation, rectified-flow interpolation, positional definitions, sampling formula and attention-complexity reasoning in Section 3 are unchanged. No mathematical results or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified video/3D modelling, arbitrary reference and target views, scaling, and zero-shot rendering quality relative to existing methods.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning texture artefacts, fixed camera intrinsics, extreme viewpoint changes and rendering speed.

D1.justification: Implementation, preprocessing, training schedules, hardware and benchmarking details in Section 4.1 and Appendices B–D are unchanged, as are project and correspondence access details. The corrected view configuration was already documented elsewhere in v2.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Adding the accent in Federico Lebrón and correcting 'Machine Laerning' to 'Machine Learning' in two references are bibliographic corrections only.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to Figure 3's caption, the bibliography corrections and updated first-page dates/version text. Sections, paragraph structure and the broader narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3's caption is corrected with slight text reflow. The chart itself and all other figures and tables retain their content, structure and placement; rendered-page comparison shows no broader layout revision.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Figure 3's misleading reversal of reference and target view counts, bringing its caption into agreement with the plot headings and Appendix A's Table 5. This improves reporting accuracy and internal consistency, alongside small bibliography corrections, while the methods and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
